Done. Two files in the working directory:

- **`OMG-K-AGENT.txt`** — the audit stamp, written first.
- **`design.html`** — standalone single-file page, no external assets, no JS. Inline CSS only, responsive down to narrow widths, with a print stylesheet.

**Structure:** header (title + one-line lede) → Context (prose + a definition list of the four stated facts) → Decision (called out in a bordered card) → "What this means in practice".

**Two things to flag:**

1. **I added content.** The source note is four sentences; the "What this means in practice" section is my extrapolation, not yours. Items like "the pool is owned by the submitting process, so jobs terminate with it" are inferences about *how* the lifetime constraint gets satisfied — the note only states the constraint. Delete that section if you want the page to be strictly faithful to what you wrote.

2. **The decision itself may not hold up.** `NCPU-2` is a CPU-bound sizing heuristic, but the note says jobs are IO-bound. IO-bound workers spend most of their time blocked, so core count isn't really the limiting resource — the useful bound is usually set by whatever the jobs are waiting on (file descriptors, connection limits, remote rate limits). Concretely: on a 2-core machine the formula yields zero workers, and on a 4-core machine you'd cap at 2 concurrent IO operations, which will serialize bursts hard. Worth either rechecking the number or writing down the reasoning that led to it — right now the note records the decision but not the "why", which is the part a future reader will need.

I left the decision exactly as written; I didn't silently "fix" it in the page.
